tossups.text: This text advises to "beat her and knock her about" when describing Fortune. This text claims that the title figure should master the conflict between cunning and strength represented by a lion and fox. This text uses the example of Cesare Borgia to argue that it is better to be feared than loved as a ruler. For 10 points, name this political text written by Niccolo Machiavelli.

In the 48th stanza of Harbard's song, this figure's reputation is assailed for supposedly having a lover at home. While not Freyr, this figure's only recorded sons are a forefather of Norse rulers who is only mentioned once in the Prose Edda and a god of hunting and archery who appropriately lives in a dwelling named after the yew tree, Ydalir. This figure was once married to the giant Orvandil, who is thought to have fathered her son Ullr. Sometimes associated with the Valkerie Hildr, this goddess has the ability to transform into a swan and is considered to be the rival of the giantess Járnsaxa, with whom this goddess' husband fathered Magni. The ship Skidbladnir and the spear Gugnir were created along with an item that would later belong to this goddess; that item was created after this figure's husband threatened Loki to replace her hair, which Loki cut off. For 10 points, name this Norse goddess, the wife of Thor who was known for her golden hair.

In human physiology, this structure is essential for defecation reflex. It plays a key role in the digestive system and is one of the most studied parts of human anatomy. For ten points, name this colon-related structure.
tossups.explanation: The colon is a key component of the Digestive system, involved in defecation reflex.

tossups.text: Near its end, a 1999 sociology book about this city claims that "old heads" want to create more men like the folkloric "Mr. Johnson," who mimicked the "decent daddy" archetype. Black folklore collected in this city is retold in Deep Down in the Jungle... by White scholar Roger Abrahams, who like Robert K. Merton was born and raised in this city. Elijah Anderson's Code of the Street is set in this city. While here, a sociologist later denied tenure by the University of Wisconsin drove a car whose other occupants intended to avenge a murdered informant dubbed "Chuck" in an area pseudonymized as "6th Street." Alice Goffman's On the Run is set in this city. An 1899 work of quantitative sociology by W. E. B. DuBois ("doo-BOYCE") described the Negro in, for 10 points, what city, whose majority-Black West section includes the University of Pennsylvania?

Every non-trivial norm on this set is either the standard absolute value or a p-adic norm according to Ostrowski's theorem. This set is the smallest field with characteristic zero. The standard method of proving this set is countable is to consider an infinite square grid and to cross out repeated elements when considering successive diagonals. For showing a number did not belong to this set, Hippasus was supposedly drowned by the Pythagoreans. The decimal expansions of elements of this set either terminate or have a repeating sequence. For 10 points, name this set denoted by a blackboard Q which is contrasted with the irrational numbers.

King Suddhodana locked this man in a palace for twenty-nine years to prevent a version of a prophecy given by a hermit seer. In the garden of Lumbini, this man emerged from under the right arm of a woman who dreamed about a white six-tusked elephant. The first sermon by this man was delivered at Deer Park after he discovered suffering in the form of a sick man, a corpse, and an ascetic. Asita prophesied that this man would become a sage or ruler before this man discovered the Middle Way. For 10 points, give the name of this "awakened one" who achieved enlightenment while sitting under a Bodhi tree, the founder of Buddhism.

A group opposed to this action was founded by the Duke of Richmond and was called CAPS. For his support of it, Charles Pelham Villiers was mocked as a "solitary Robinson Crusoe." The Earl of Derby resigned for the second time as Colonial Secretary in protest of this action. The author of Factories and the Factory System, William Cooke Taylor, was a propagandist for this cause, which finally succeeded the same night a Prime Minister's Irish Coercion Bill failed to pass, prompting that man's resignation. A league advocating for this action was founded by John Bright and Richard Cobden and helped found The Economist to support it. Proponents of this cause utilized the writings of David Ricardo. For 10 points, name this action finally implemented in the final days of the Robert Peel ministry, which removed certain laws designed to protect British grain producers.

A character in this novel believes that watches are "silly gadgets" and keeps time by transferring peas between two jars constantly. At the conclusion of this novel, a dragged-looking spaniel "somersaults like a pancake" after it is shot by a character whose shooting rampage kills nothing but the dog. An actor dies on stage while performing Orpheus and Eurydice in this novel, in which the magistrate Othon creates isolation camps. The journalist Raymond Rambert tries to flee from the setting of this novel, where Cottard is a smuggler of black market goods. Thousands of rats die in the streets of Oran at the opening of this novel. For 10 points, Doctor Bernard Rieux is the protagonist of what novel by Albert Camus, named for a disease?

In the Platonic dialogue named after a disciple of this man, the title character renounces speech in favor of finger wagging because he's convinced words aren't reliable; that disciple was Cratylus. This Greek philosopher was a strong proponent of dialectical monism, partially due to his belief that up and down were the same. This man was characterized by some of his contemporaries as "the weeping philosopher." This philosopher considered fire to be the most fundamental element. He was the first philosopher to deal seriously with the concept of logos, and his philosophy of change can be summed up by the aphorism panta rhei, or "everything flows." For 10 points, who is this Greek philosopher who is perhaps best known for saying that a man can't step in the same river twice?

One person of this last name born with the last name Epps worked for her husband's father at the Tigoni Primate Research Center, Meave. That husband led the first expedition to Koobi Fora and took part in the discovery of the Turkana Boy. In addition to Richard, another couple of this last name, his parents, are known for work in Tanzania. For 10 points, name this family of social scientists that includes Mary and Louis, known for finding hominid fossils in the Olduvai Gorge.

MODERATOR NOTE: Make clear that "Greatest Snow on Earth" is in quotes. In 1964, this body of water was separated from the artificial reservoir Willard Bay. The Weber River, which is home to mountain whitefish, empties into this body of water. An effect named for this body of water causes the "Greatest Snow on Earth," and Pink Floyd was a flamingo often seen near this body of water. Robert Smithson created Spiral Jetty on the shores of this body of water. The so-called "golden spike" was originally located just north of this body of water, and this body of water is all that remains of Lake Bonneville. For 10 points, name this lake in the Western United States, the namesake of a city in Utah.
acceptableAnswers: Great Salt until “lake” and accept after

tossups.text: This poet lamented "the veil so governs me that to my death, and by heat and cold, the sweet light of your lovely eyes is shadowed." To begin a collection, this poet wrote that he has "become an old tale" such that "shame is the fruit of [his] vanities." This poet lyrically prostrates himself before a figure who is "filled with every grace" and "clothed in glory, crowned with stars" before asking her to send him to her son, Jesus Christ. This poet describes how love found him "all weaponless" upon being spellbound by "lovely eyes" "on that day when the sun's ray / was darkened." This author opens one collection by calling to "you who hear the sound, in scattered rhymes." For 10 points, name this admirer of Laura, the Italian poet of Il Canzoniere and namesake of a sonnet style.

One leader of this country organized the Blue Division, and this was led by Miguel Primo de Rivera and Juan Negrin. The Abraham Lincoln Brigades and the Condor Legion fought in this country. A civil war in this country saw the Carlists side the with the Phalange, and one leader of this country suppressed minority languages like Galician and Basque. For 10 points, name this Iberian country long led by Francisco Franco.

These events can be referred to as "the dance of Inanna." The "garden of the Badb" was used as an epithet for sites of these events, which were frequented by a triple goddess whose aspects include Macha and Nemain. That goddess often appears at these events in the form of a hoarse-voiced bird. Enyo is said to be "supreme" in this event, whose outcomes are prophesied by the Morrigan. Eris can also often be found near these events. A lost statue depicted Nike in the hand of a wise goddess of this domain, who is often shown holding her aegis and spear. For 10 points, name this domain governed by goddesses like Bellona and Athena.
acceptableAnswers: strife by asking “what does it lead to?”

tossups.text: At the end of a play by this author, a character advances to the front of the stage and asks the audience's forgiveness by saying, "I put myself on you that are my country." Several plays by this author start with an "Argument," or an acrostic poem giving the play's title. In a play by this author, the gullible gambler Dapper and tobacconist Drugger are conned. In another play by this man, an aging nobleman fakes an illness in order to receive lavish gifts from characters like Corbaccio and Corvino; that play's title character, a Venetian nobleman, attempts to rape Celia, and is assisted by the servant Mosca. For 10 points, name this 17th-century English author of The Alchemist and Volpone .

This anatomical structure, studied extensively in clinical medicine, this structure is essential for muscle fiber types. It plays a key role in the musculoskeletal system and is one of the most studied parts of human anatomy. For ten points, name this sarcomere-related structure.
tossups.explanation: The sarcomere is a key component of the Musculoskeletal system, involved in muscle fiber types.

tossups.text: Used in the eighteenth century for the treatment of edema by the botanist William Withering, the active steroids in this substance are cardiac glycosides. For 10 points-name this drug that strengthens the contractions of the heart muscle and is obtained from the foxglove plant.

This anatomical structure, studied extensively in clinical medicine, this structure is essential for thyroid hormones t3 and t4. It plays a key role in the endocrine system and is one of the most studied parts of human anatomy. For ten points, name this thyroid-related structure.
tossups.explanation: The thyroid is a key component of the Endocrine system, involved in thyroid hormones t3 and t4.

tossups.text: Soldiers from this polity were sent to assist the Ionian Revolt. This polity's control of the silver mines of Laurium allowed it to construct a massive fleet, with which it controlled the Delian League. This polity's port of Piraeus was protected by its famous Long Walls, inside of which, the Funeral Oration of Pericles, a leader of this polity, was given. The victor at the Battle of Salamis, Themistocles, was a general from this polity, which lost one conflict following the Battle of Aegospotami. For 10 points, name this Ancient Greek city-state, which fought the Peloponnesian War with Sparta, and which is the modern-day capital of Greece.

This place is the setting of the poem "Paradise Lost" by John Milton. Mormons believe that this place is located in Jackson County, Missouri. God placed a special tree and a serpent in this place. For 10 points, name this place where Adam and Eve disobeyed God after eating a piece of Forbidden Fruit.

parts.text: Name this Hindu preserver deity who is often depicted holding a conch and mace in two of his four hands. This god is considered the supreme deity in the Vaishnavist sect of Hinduism.
The seventh avatar of Vishnu is this figure, who rescues his wife Sita from the demon Ravana in a Hindu epic named for him.
acceptableAnswers: the Ramayana by asking “what is the name of that work’s main character?

parts.text: In a Vedic myth, Vishnu covers all of the heavens in only this many steps. The Tridevi is a group of this many Hindu gods, and the Christian Holy Trinity describes this many aspects of God.

bonuses.leadin: The Alvars were a group of Tamil saints famed for their devotion to this deity. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Identify this Slavic fertility god who, in an uncannily similar story to the myth of Persephone, is stolen from his father by Veles, then taken to the underworld.
Jarilo's father was this chief Slavic god, who caused thunder and lightning, and tossed his hammer at wrongdoers.
Afer the Slavs were Christianized, Jarilo was identifed with this patron saint of England, who killed a dragon.

bonuses.leadin: Though this god was ritually dismembered in the underworld, he nonetheless inaugurated spring by riding back to earth on a white horse. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name the primary structure associated with lymph nodes and vessels.
What is the main function of the lymph in the immune system?
Name another component of the immune system related to lymph nodes and vessels.

bonuses.leadin: For 10 points each, answer these questions about the human immune system.

parts.text: Name this anthropologist who argued for the primacy of violence among the Yanomami, whom he called the "Fierce People."

In Darkness in El Dorado, Patrick Tierney claimed Chagnon and this geneticist introduced a vaccine that badly intensified a measles epidemic among the Yanomamo. This pioneer of human genetics also proposed the "thrifty gene" hypothesis to explain the evolutionary presence of diabetes.
Yanomamo culture is one of the best-preserved examples of life from this period. It is commonly divided into the Paleolithic, Mesolithic, and Neolithic eras.

bonuses.leadin: This anthropologist was criticized for offering indigenous people machetes in order to film their social practices. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Linear momentum is normally a three-vector; to make a four-vector out of it, you have to add this quantity divided by the speed of light.

The conservation of linear momentum is embodied in this law of motion, which states that a body at rest will remain at rest, and a body in motion will move with constant velocity, unless acted upon by an external force.

These solutions to the Schrodinger equation are eigenstates of the momentum operator, as they are states with a single defined momentum. As a result, they are spread out over all space and are non-normalizable.

bonuses.leadin: Answer the following about everyone's favorite conserved quantity, linear momentum For 10 points each.

parts.text: Name this Muslim prophet, the father of Ishmael.
Ishmael got left in the desert while Hagar looked for water by running up and down the hills al-Safa and al-Marwah. Mother and son were saved when God created this well for them.
After drinking from the Well of Zamzam to commemorate Hagar, participants in the Hajj undertake a vigil on this hill where Muhammad gave his Farewell Sermon.

bonuses.leadin: God commanded fire temporarily not to be hot after this man's tormentors threw him into one. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this man who supervised the rebuilding of his home city of Miletus before drawing up a namesake grid plan that was deployed to build Piraeus and many other classical cities.

Hippodamus was hired to plan the grid layout of this city, which Pericles founded on the site of Sybaris as a panhellenic instead of Athenian colony. Herodotus and the orator Lysias were among the Greeks to migrate to this city in Magna Graecia.

Hippodamian grids influenced early modern city planning via this Roman's adaption of the idea in his Ten Books on Architecture. His work contains a description of ideal proportions that imagines a human body inscribed in a circle.

bonuses.leadin: Along with a law passed by the city of Sybaris, one of this man's writings is cited as an early description of patent law. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name these automatons that are said to have "positronic brains," according to Asimov.
This Czech science fiction writer wrote about robots taking over the world in his play R.U.R, which introduced the word "robot."

In another play by Čapek titled for the war with these animals, Captain van Toch enslaves a race of these intelligent amphibians for pearl fishing. These animals demand lebensraum and destroy Earth's landmass.

bonuses.leadin: The Zeroth law of these objects, created by Isaac Asimov, states that they "may not harm humanity." For 10 points each:

parts.text: This text argues that gunas can only affect the ego and have no impact on the spirit. This text outlines the three yoga paths to obtain moksha as jñana ("NYAH-nuh"), bhakti, and karma.

The Bhagavad Gita is framed as a dialogue between Krishna and Arjuna as the latter determines whether to participate in one of these events due to the loss of life it will cause. St. Augustine provided the first defense for the "just" form of these events.

The Bhagavad Gita was consolidated into the doctrine of Advaita Vedanta by this philosopher. This philosopher argued for the unity of Atman and Nigurna Brahman, and discussed the nature of a "brahman without attributes."

bonuses.leadin: This text recommends "inner renunciation" in pursuing an active life to fulfill dharma. Commentaries on this work often synthesize bhakti into the Vedanta school. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this concept, used as a medium of exchange goods and services. The use of this concept in the market replaced bartering.
This economist wrote a Treatise on Money in addition to the influential General Theory of Employment, Interest and Money. He advocated government spending to fight the effects of economic downturns.
Keynes lead the British delegation to this 1944 economic conference in New Hampshire. It established the IMF and established guidelines for the system of currency exchange rates.

bonuses.leadin: The fiat type of this concept is imbued with value by a government's declaration. For 10 points each,

parts.text: Name this European island on the west side of a waterway called the Great Belt, south of the Skagerrak strait. A suspension bridge across the Great Belt links it to Zealand to its east.
Fyn lies east of Jutland in this Scandinavian nation.

Denmark contains a district named for these features, where the S.S. Hjeljen has been in continuous operation near Silkeborg since 1861. Another district named for them overlaps with northwestern Patagonia in Argentina, and a third in northern England inspired poets such as Robert Southey.

bonuses.leadin: This island's largest city, Odense, preserves the childhood home of Hans Christian Andersen. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this religious group depicted in Miriam Toews's ("taves's") novels Women Talking and Irma Voth, which was inspired by her film role as a member of this group. The narrator of Denis Johnson's "Beverly Home" spies on a couple from this religious group.
Like Women Talking, this 2019 novel depicts a woman in a bonnet on its cover. Aunt Lydia describes her work in the Mayday resistance movement in Gilead in one part of this novel.
This author of The Testaments described the subject matter of Miriam Toews's Women Talking as "something out of" her own novel, The Handmaid's Tale.

bonuses.leadin: The image of an underwater river in the Black Sea reoccurs in a novel in which women from this religious group meet in a hayloft to discuss a series of sexual assaults. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this African country that lies on the Cape of Good Hope whose three capitals are Bloemfontein, Pretoria, and Cape Town and whose largest city is Johannesburg.
This country with capital at Maseru lies entirely within South Africa. Almost 25% of its population is infected with HIV and Letsie III is this country's reigning king.

The longest river in South Africa has this name. A county by this name directly south of Los Angeles includes the cities of Anaheim, Huntington Beach, and Fullerton, in addition to being the site of Disneyland.

bonuses.leadin: This country has eleven official languages, including Afrikaans. For 10 points each:

parts.text: This Inca sun god was frequently depicted as a sun-disk, which appears on the flags of Peru and Argentina. He was married to his sister, the moon goddess Mama Killa.
Sun gods of this country's mythology include Aten, around whom Akhenaten focused a new religion, and another named Ra.
This sun goddess birthed three women from the sword of her brother, Susano-o, but angrily claimed that they belonged to Susano-o when he upstaged her by birthing five men from her necklace.

bonuses.leadin: Here comes the sun! For 10 points each, name some sun deities.

parts.text: Name this author, whose novel The Member of the Wedding follows the tomboy Frankie Addams. A more famous novel by this author features the deaf-mute John Singer.
This author called Clock Without Hands, a McCullers novel, "the worst book I have ever read." The Misfit murders the Grandmother in her story "A Good Man is Hard to Find."
McCullers and O'Connor were both female members of this literary tradition, which uses slightly disturbing or sinister elements in works that are set in the namesake part of the United States.

bonuses.leadin: This author included "Wunderkind" in The Ballad of the Sad Cafe. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name the primary structure associated with blood vessel structure.
What is the main function of the aorta in the cardiovascular system?
Name another component of the cardiovascular system related to blood vessel structure.

bonuses.leadin: For 10 points each, answer these questions about the human cardiovascular system.

parts.text: Name this type of scattering which is responsible for the blue color of the sky, in which the particles that scatter the light are much smaller than the wavelength of light and have refractive indices close to one.

When particle size approaches wavelength size, this other kind of scattering named for a German physicist occurs, provided that the particles are spherical. This computational method uses the electric and magnetic fields of the dielectric sphere to determine how much the light is scattered and where it goes.

Rayleigh scattering and Mie scattering are two examples of this type of scattering in which the kinetic energy of the particles is conserved, and thus the wavelength of scattered light is the same as that of the incident light.

bonuses.leadin: Why is the sky blue? For 10 points each,

parts.text: Name the primary structure associated with colon sections.
What is the main function of the colon in the digestive system?
Name another component of the digestive system related to colon sections.

bonuses.leadin: For 10 points each, answer these questions about the human digestive system.

parts.text: Give this name of a king who lost the Great Northern War to Peter the Great. He was the twelfth king of his country with that name.

A later king of that country, Gustavus Adolphus, took part in this war. This war, named for its length, began after the Second Defenestration of Prague, and saw Gustavus Adolphus die in the battle of Lutzen.
Charles XII and Gustavus Adolphus were both kings of this Scandinavian country, whose modern-day capital is Stockholm.

bonuses.leadin: A king of this name fled to the Ottoman Empire during a war in which he lost the battle of Poltava. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this artist whose silkscreen depictions of everyday objects include Green Coca-Cola Bottles and Campbell's Soup Cans.
Warhol was a member of this 1950's and 1960's art movement that used objects of mass culture for its subjects and styles.
Warhol produced a diptych (DIP-tik) based on the face of this actress, who starred in Some Like it Hot and The Seven Year Itch.

bonuses.leadin: This man's studio was known as "The Factory". For 10 points each:
